review.rationale: The title-winning 2010 core is well represented, with Dhoni keeping, four overseas players, strong top-order continuity, and more than five deployment units.
The championship season supplies the Gilchrist-led batting core and a legal four-overseas XI; Ojha and RP Singh anchor a multi-option attack.
The table-leading 2009 side has a credible Sehwag-Gambhir-de Villiers top order, Karthik keeping, three overseas players, and five deployable bowling options.
The strongest KKR Foundation candidate retains the Ganguly-Gayle core, Saha as keeper, only three overseas players, and complete pace-spin deployment capacity despite weaker historical performance.
The finalist 2010 XI has Tendulkar, Pollard and Malinga, four overseas players, a legitimate keeper-capable selection, and balanced five-unit bowling deployment.
The 2008 semifinalist preserves the Marsh-Sangakkara-Yuvraj batting identity, uses exactly four overseas players, and has full bowling deployment coverage.
The inaugural champion is the clearest Foundation representative, with Smith, Watson, Pathan and Warne, a legal overseas count, keeper coverage, and the strongest reviewed V2 bowling mark.
The 2010 playoff side provides Kallis, Pietersen, Kohli and a proven Kumble-Steyn attack, with a confirmed keeper, four overseas players, and full deployment capacity.
